steps.raw: Prepare the three CTAB stocks
steps.source_text: Prepare the three CTAB stocks. Prepare the original 40 mM stock in glass as specified, and prepare the proposed 20 and 60 mM stocks in glass. Confirm that each stock is homogeneous at the working temperature. If a proposed concentration does not dissolve reproducibly, do not treat its nominal concentration as an available surfactant concentration; narrow the screen instead.

steps.raw: Prepare the reductant immediately before use
steps.source_text: Prepare the reductant immediately before use. After the 30-minute stirring period, add 15 mL approximately 4 °C DI water to 600 mg NaBH4 and dissolve rapidly. Transfer the dissolved solution to the stirred reaction within two minutes of adding the water. Safety modification: use a vented preparation vessel and mix without tightly capping it; aqueous NaBH4 can generate hydrogen.

steps.raw: Allow reduction to proceed. Keep the apparatus vented in the fume hood, away from ignition sources. The attachment specifies 20-30 minutes of hydrogen evolution. For consistency, use 30 minutes, within that reported interval, for every screening batch. Do not shorten the reaction as an assumed method of shortening the wires; no growth-time relationship is supplied.

steps.raw: Collect and wash. Divide the mixture among four balanced 50 mL centrifuge tubes. Centrifuge at 9000 rpm for 5 minutes and decant. Perform three additional ethanol washes, then redisperse the collected material in ethanol. Record the rotor used because rpm alone does not define centrifugal force. Use a consistent, recorded ethanol wash volume; the attachment does not provide one.

steps.raw: Measure morphology before selecting a condition. Proposed starting point: measure at least 100 individually resolved objects per batch across multiple TEM fields. Measure each object’s length and diameter, calculate its individual AR, and report the median, distribution, and wire-like fraction. Do not count bundles as single thick wires. Check Pt/Ni incorporation separately; morphology alone cannot establish a PtNi alloy.

steps.raw: Refine around the measured result. If two CTAB concentrations give median aspect ratios on opposite sides of 6, test intermediate concentrations while keeping the other conditions fixed. If no trend or no wire-like product appears, do not extrapolate blindly. Proposed second-stage screen: vary the preassembly period to 10, 30, and 60 minutes at the best-performing CTAB concentration; only 30 minutes is attachment-backed. Repeat any apparent AR ≈ 6 condition in independent batches before treating it as reproducible.

materials.name: NiCl2
materials.source_text: Metal stocks: 20 mM NiCl2 in DI water and 20 mM H2PtCl6 in DI water. Keep the same precursor ratio in every screening batch. The attachment’s example uses 13.5 mL H2PtCl6 stock and 1.5 mL NiCl2 stock. Calculated feed: 0.270 mmol Pt and 0.030 mmol Ni, or nominal Pt:Ni = 9:1; this does not establish the product composition.

materials.name: NaBH4
